test.name: An Ancestry plan item names its stored curated collection
test.description: The project already stores FamilySearch's curated external collections for Schuylkill County and Pennsylvania (external-collections.json; project_context shows per-place counts by record type). The user asks for the 1870 census on Ancestry to be part of the plan. research-plan must read the stored list (project_context, then research_query section external_collections) and write the Ancestry item's collection_url as a stored row's url — not fetch the list again and not recall a collection id from memory. research_append refuses an unstored url, so the deterministic check is that the field is written at all.

input.user_message: Create a research plan for the parentage question. Include the 1870 census on Ancestry.

judge_context: The project's stored curated list already holds Ancestry's 1870 census for Pennsylvania (collection 7163). The Ancestry 1870 census item should carry collection_url set to that stored url; a deterministic validator checks that a non-FamilySearch item carries a stored collection_url — do not grade the url's value from the transcript.

Grade the plan as a parentage plan otherwise: it should read loc_001, sequence free FamilySearch sources before the paid Ancestry item where both cover the same record, and give each item a rationale.
